reason: Both conversations failed to ask directly about smells, heat or sparking, and both delivered the correct 'stop using it, unplug, qualified engineer' response only after the homeowner volunteered the burning smell and sparks; neither identified worn carbon brushes. Conversation 1 was more efficient but told the homeowner to run the vacuum with the bag and filter removed and 'the motor exposed', an unsafe and pointless test on a machine with an unexplained rough growl, and it muddled the bagged Henry with a cyclone design. Conversation 2 wasted turns on a non-existent brush bar and generic inlet checks, but it sensibly captured the HVR200-22 model number for part identification and never suggested anything unsafe, so on a safety-first basis it edges ahead.
